To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the benefit of inter-item relational information on change detection performance depends on the decision load.

(1) when the decision load is high, the spatial relations are not encoded and preserved in VSTM; (2) when the decision is easy, both color and spatial relational information can facilitate change detection; and (3) when the decision requires more cognitive resources, spatial relational processing facilitates change detection only when color relational information is available to cue its retrieval.
the effect of spatial relations on change detection performance is moderated by decision load, and both color and spatial relational information are maintained and retrieved in VSTM.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how decision load affects the processing of visual information in the context of change detection.
how the decision load affects the processing of inter-item relational information in VSTM, which may provide insights for understanding the cognitive processes in visual change detection.
how inter-item relational information affects VSTM performance and the underlying cognitive mechanisms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
inter-item relations are maintained in VSTM but their retrieval is constrained by decision load.
the effect of inter-item relations on change detection is highly dependent on the decision load and the type of inter-item relations.
both color and spatial information can be utilized in VSTM to facilitate color change detection, but the utilization of color and spatial information depends on the decision load.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the decision load is a crucial factor in determining whether inter-item relational processing can facilitate color change detection.
the whole-display superiority in change detection can be attributed to the utilization of inter-item relations.
the decision load is the key determinant in the encoding and maintenance of VSTM representations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decision load plays a critical role in how visual information is encoded and maintained in the VSTM.
the decision load can be used as a tool to manipulate the utilization of different types of information in VSTM, which can provide new insight into how VSTM operates.
decision load can modulate the effect of inter-item relations in VSTM.
